clue.text: Women raped in base manoeuvre

indicators.note: to manoeuvre is to move things around, so these letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Something nasty is done to women during a military exercise at a base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvre' rearranges the letters of IN BASE. The legend of the rape of the Sabine women tells of their abduction by the early Romans.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman legend the women of a neighbouring tribe were seized by Romulus's men, an episode called the Rape of the Sabine Women.

clue.text: Led astray, being partly schooled in a third of 22

indicators.note: the shortened word for schooled is placed inside the letters from 22

parts.note: 22-across has nine letters; its first three, a third of the whole, are S, E, D

indicators.note: only part of the synonym is used, its first four letters

parts.note: schooled means educated

explanation.surface: Someone has been tempted, perhaps by a partial education in a cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: 22-across is SEDGEMOOR, so its first third is SED; 'partly' keeps only the start of EDUCATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be seduced is to be led astray or tempted into wrongdoing, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Sort of speech dished up, say, by a political party

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means turned upward, so the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated EG
the Liberals, abbreviated LIB, are a British political party

explanation.surface: A party serves up a certain kind of political speech.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'dished up' reads the pieces upwards. 'Sort of speech' is used disparagingly: bilge is drivel.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilge is worthless talk or nonsense, so it is a kind of speech in a scornful sense.

clue.text: Reported man of rank mounted is a horrific experience

indicators.note: reported means heard rather than seen, so the title is taken by its sound

parts.note: a knight is a man holding a rank of honour
a mare is a female horse, something a rider mounts

explanation.surface: A mounted nobleman is said to be terrifying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reported' applies only to the man of rank; a mounted knight sits on his horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare is a frightening dream, and by extension any horrific experience.

clue.text: One may be in or out

definitions.text: One may be in or out

parts.words: One may be in or out
parts.note: in cricket the batsman facing the bowling is in, while a worker who has downed tools is out on strike

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman facing the bowling is the one who is 'in'; a worker on strike is 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: The batsman receiving the ball in cricket bears this name, as does a worker who has walked out.

clue.text: Body builder gets one sorted out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A bodybuilder gets someone sorted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges I (one) with SORTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabolic steroids are drugs used to build muscle, so the substance is a builder of bodies.

clue.text: Theatrical show always turns over a turn

indicators.note: the reversed word covers a letter, so it is put around it
turns tells us to read the word for always backwards

parts.note: always means ever
a U-turn is a turn, giving U

explanation.surface: A stage show is forever doing the same comic turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses EVER to REVE, and 'over' puts it around U (as in U-turn).
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a light theatrical entertainment of sketches, songs and dances.

clue.text: Irish resort to rid western state of its governor

parts.note: ridding a place of someone, in this pun, means to kill him
the governor of California when the clue appeared was Arnold Schwarzenegger, known as Arnie, here spelt as it is pronounced

explanation.surface: An Irish holiday town resorts to removing an American governor.
explanation.walkthrough: A punning clue: ridding California of Arnie (Arnold Schwarzenegger) would be to 'kill Arnie', which sounds like the Irish town. The spelling of ARNEY is bent to fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Killarney in County Kerry is a well-known Irish tourist town by the lakes.

clue.text: Sex Pistol = 2 + 10

parts.note: points to the answer at 2-down, which means nonsense, or rot
the number ten spelt out

explanation.surface: A punk musician is summed up as an equation.
explanation.walkthrough: Johnny Rotten was the singer of the Sex Pistols, a 1970s punk band.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnny Rotten (John Lydon) was lead singer of the punk group, so he is one of its members.

clue.text: Take in how many a true word is spoken (sic)

indicators.note: sic admits the spelling is wrong, telling us the phrase is taken by its sound only

parts.words: how many a true word is spoken
parts.note: the proverb says many a true word is spoken in jest

explanation.surface: A proverb is quoted, with an apology for its spelling.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'many a true word is spoken in jest' supplies IN JEST, which sounds like the answer; '(sic)' flags the deliberate misspelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food or drink into the body, so to take in.

clue.text: Transport application

definitions.meaning: a public stagecoach, especially in France, was called by this name
steady effort and care in work

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a French stagecoach and careful persistent effort, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Servant takes time to say goodbye

parts.note: vale is the Latin farewell

explanation.surface: A servant takes a moment to bid farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' simply joins the Latin farewell VALE to T.
explanation.definitionFit: A valet is a manservant who looks after a man's clothes and personal needs.

clue.text: Falsify the account?

parts.note: cooking the books or telling a false story both deceive, read as one action

explanation.definitionFit: To deceive or act dishonestly, as in fiddling a financial record.

clue.text: Acquit without a single charge

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
a single thing is one
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: Someone is cleared with no charge at all.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to clear someone of blame, which is to acquit.

clue.text: Many find native dancing unorthodox

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Many people consider indigenous dancing out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' giving D is a crossword convention: D is the Roman numeral for 500.
explanation.definitionFit: Deviant means departing from accepted norms, so unorthodox.

clue.text: Dicky loved city with a cycle track

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for shaky or unsound, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: Rome is a city

explanation.surface: Someone with a weak heart loved a city that has a cycling stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' (British slang for unreliable, as in a dicky heart) rearranges LOVED to VELOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A velodrome is an arena with a banked track for cycle racing.

clue.text: Gee, it's a bit of a fag

definitions.meaning: the letter G is the end of the word dog
fag is British slang for cigarette; a stub is what remains of one

explanation.walkthrough: 'fag' is British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigarette stub is called this in British slang, and the last letter of the canine word is G.

clue.text: Fish has a smoke by water at Calais

parts.note: gasper is old British slang for a cheap cigarette
eau is the French for water, and Calais is in France

explanation.surface: A fish has a cigarette beside the sea in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The gaspereau is a North American fish, the alewife, a kind of herring.

clue.text: Premier of "La Forza del Destino"?

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters taken from the title

explanation.surface: Asks about the first performance of a Verdi opera.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in 'dEL DESTino'. 'Premier' means first, and the eldest child is the first born.
explanation.definitionFit: Premier means first, and the eldest is the first-born of a family.

clue.text: Commissioner of Oaths?

parts.note: a legal official who administers oaths, reread as someone who commits profanities, as in to swear like a cavalry soldier

explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'swear like a ...' makes this soldier a famous committer of oaths, punning on the legal title.

clue.text: Tried to spread seed around, for example

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed around the abbreviation word
spread letters are scattered and reformed

parts.note: say means for example

explanation.surface: A gardener attempts to scatter seed all round, as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges SEED to ESED, and 'around' wraps it round the synonym for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: Essayed is a formal word for attempted or tried.

clue.text: New parent in ecstasy

indicators.note: new gives a fresh arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A new parent is overjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges PARENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrapt means carried away with delight, so in a state of ecstasy.

clue.text: One entertained by vagrant, which could be dodgy

indicators.note: one guest is entertained inside a host, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: dosser is British slang for a homeless vagrant
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone taken in by a tramp could be shady.
explanation.walkthrough: Recalls the 2003 'dodgy dossier' used by the British government to make its case for the Iraq war.
explanation.definitionFit: A file of documents, famously called dodgy when the UK's 2003 Iraq briefing was found to be plagiarised.

clue.text: They quiver like writers

parts.note: as means like
pens are writing tools

explanation.surface: Writers tremble.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspens are poplars whose leaves tremble in the slightest breeze.

clue.text: Back-room boy, say, in battle

indicators.note: back tells us to read the whole run of pieces from the end

parts.note: room taken as written
a boy, for example Des, written out as E.G. DES

explanation.surface: A back-room boy fought in a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns ROOM plus EG DES into one backward run. Sedgemoor (1685) in Somerset was the last pitched battle on English soil.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Sedgemoor in Somerset ended the Monmouth Rebellion in 1685.

clue.text: Rusbridger retains people to do this

indicators.note: the editor holds the people within

parts.note: Alan Rusbridger was then editor of the Guardian, abbreviated ED
men are people

explanation.surface: The newspaper's editor keeps staff to make corrections.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Rusbridger edited the Guardian, where the puzzle appeared; editing copy is his job.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct a text, which is what an editor and his staff do.

clue.text: Refuse collector possibly loses head in Ireland

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Dennis is a British maker of dustcarts, the vehicles that collect refuse

explanation.surface: A binman may lose his head in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Dennis is a British maker of dustcarts (refuse lorries). Ennis is the county town of Clare.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennis is a town found in Ireland, the county town of County Clare.

clue.text: One so corrupt is for hanging

indicators.note: corrupt letters are spoilt and mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone so corrupt deserves to hang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges ONE SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a rope loop used for hanging someone.

clue.text: To start with, English railway lines deteriorate

indicators.note: the first letters of the next two words are taken

parts.note: an ode is a poem, lines of verse

explanation.surface: English railway lines have been decaying from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To start with' takes E and R, then ODE.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, so to deteriorate.

clue.text: Go to Evita with one sausage

parts.note: go means energy, pep
Eva Peron was known as Evita
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone goes with a friend to see the musical Evita, and buys a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy Italian dried sausage.

clue.text: Spare a bob — by one having plenty to spare

parts.note: a bob was a shilling in British pre-decimal money, abbreviated S
a lender has money to spare

explanation.surface: A beggar asks for a shilling from someone with plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was the old British shilling, written S.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare as an adjective means thin, lean, which is slender.

clue.text: Heartless arrogance of film director

indicators.note: H stands for hearts in card notation, so without hearts the H goes

parts.note: hauteur is haughty arrogance

explanation.surface: A heartless, arrogant film director.
explanation.definitionFit: An auteur is a film director with a strong personal style.
